extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, judges, and law students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how courts of equity grant, continue, or dissolve injunctions in patent-infringement suits, including who may sue, what the bill should contain, procedural prerequisites (notice, affidavits), and the factual standards the court weighs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties entitled to relief in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties entitled to relief in equity against the infringement of a patent are the party or parties interested in the patent — whether patentee, assignees, or grantees of the exclusive right for a particular district — i.e., any person holding the legal title or the right to bring an action may bring a bill for an injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the assignee has the whole interest he may sue alone; if he has less than the whole interest he must join the patentee. If an assignment has not been recorded, the assignee is not substituted to the right and responsibility of the patentee so as to maintain any suit in law or equity. In a joint suit by patentee and assignee, a disclaimer filed by the patentee which the assignee does not join cannot operate in favor of the complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee for a particular district / joinder in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantee of an exclusive right for a particular district may bring an action at law within his own district; in equity the patentee may be joined with the assignee of such a limited district right because the patentee retains an interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantee limited to use of a specified number of machines in a town has an exclusive right within that territory and may maintain an action in his own name. Different persons who have infringed independently cannot be made defendants in the same bill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the bill for injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill for an injunction should recite the application for the letters-patent, compliance with prerequisites, the issue of the letters (giving the title verbatim), attestation and delivery, and should make profert of the letters; it need not set forth the description in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bill must state that the plaintiff, after issuance, put the invention into use and is at filing in the exclusive possession of it. If brought on assignee title, renewal, extension, amendment, or disclaimer, those facts should be set forth to show present state of title. The bill should state the infringement (actual or threatened), any prior actions or injunctions, that the defendant was requested to desist and to account, and (if relevant) charges of combination or conspiracy. The prayer should seek discovery on oath, particular answers to interrogatories, a general answer, decree for gains and profits, an injunction to restrain further use, delivery or destruction of infringing machines, further relief, a writ of injunction and a subpoena. The bill should be sworn to by affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of surrender and renewal during pending injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent is surrendered and renewed pending proceedings, a supplemental bill is necessary to continue a temporary injunction as to the new patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a temporary injunction was granted on the original bill and the patent is surrendered and a new patent issued, a supplemental bill (naming the new patent) should be filed to continue the injunction as to the new patent until hearing or further order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of originality / usual affidavits on motion
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain an injunction the plaintiff should accompany his application with an affidavit that he believes himself to be the original and first inventor, and similar affidavits are commonly read when moving for an injunction before answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances subsequent to procurement of the patent may reveal the patentee was mistaken; a special affidavit to that effect was required by some judges and is usual practice on motion for injunction prior to answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement before applying for injunction (U.S. courts)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the courts of the United States, notice that an injunction is to be applied for must be served on the defendant; no injunction (temporary or final) can be granted without reasonable previous notice of the time and place of moving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule means injunctions in patent cases are not granted ex parte without notice; motions may be made on filing and before answer but only with prior notice to the adverse party or their attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: No ex parte injunctions in patent cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Injunctions are not granted on ex parte applications in patent cases, although they may be granted on filing and before answer on notice, and also after answer and upon hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where the bill is sworn when filed, the courts insist on notice; the equitable power to grant injunctions is exercised according to well-settled equitable rules and reasonable application to the case's facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: When court will grant injunction without prior action at law (Lord Eldon rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent has been granted and there has been an exclusive possession of some duration under it, the court will interpose its injunction without putting the party previously to establish validity by an action at law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent is recent ('of yesterday') and validity is strongly challenged (e.g., defective specification), the court will not decide validity on its own but will send the patentee to law to establish the patent before granting injunctive relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear right with affidavit supports injunction pre-trial
rubrics_metrics.description: If the bill states a clear right and the allegation is verified by affidavit (including evidence of exclusive possession or use), the court will grant an injunction and continue it until hearing without sending the plaintiff to law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear right can be shown by use or sale (part or whole) or long enjoyment; however, if there are reasonable doubts about validity, the court will require a trial at law (sometimes expedited) and may permit the plaintiff to return for an account if the law trial is in his favor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three evidentiary contexts for deciding whether to require law trial
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule about sending the plaintiff to law must be subdivided by the aspect of the case: (1) where only the bill and affidavits are before the court; (2) where the injunction is asked before final hearing but respondent offers evidence in answer/affidavits; (3) where the question comes on at the hearing with full proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different proof thresholds apply in each class: see the separate criteria for class (1) and (2) below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class (1) — bill and affidavits only: required showing
rubrics_metrics.description: When injunction is sought on the bill and affidavits alone, the bill and affidavits must show issuance of the patent and an exclusive possession of the right of some duration; these will ordinarily support granting an injunction absent glaring defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent contains glaring defects or the bill is materially defective, the injunction will be refused and plaintiff sent to law. Additional helpful evidence includes the patentee having used the invention undisturbed for some time and prior successful prosecutions against others (length of enjoyment strengthens the presumption of validity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class (2) — opposing evidence before hearing: factors to weigh
rubrics_metrics.description: Where opposing evidence is adduced before the hearing, the court weighs how long and how exclusively the right has been exercised, how far the respondent has raised doubts as to novelty, patentability, or infringement, and whether long possession counteracts evidence impeaching validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is prima facie right to an injunction where there is a patent, long possession, and infringement; the court must judge whether the respondent's evidence has displaced that prima facie right sufficiently to suspend the injunction pending a law trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of long enjoyment and prior recoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: When presumption in favor of validity is strengthened by long enjoyment, undisturbed possession for several years, and recoveries against other alleged infringers, it will not be sufficient for defendant to read affidavits casting doubt on originality to deprive the plaintiff of an injunction before a trial at law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long enjoyment and prior recoveries are powerful corroborative evidence of a probable right; mere affidavit evidence tending to impeach originality may be overcome by such historic enjoyment and enforcement.
